topic: Common Ion Effect and Hydrolysis of Salts
title: Common Ion, Salt Hydrolysis Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Table salt in water stays neutral, washing soda water feels slippery and ammonium chloride water turns a little sour. All three are salts, so why are they not all neutral? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Diya cleans the floor with washing soda and her fingers feel slippery.

On the molecule bench you will watch sodium acetate pour a crowd of acetate ions into acetic acid: acetate grabs hydronium, the equilibrium shifts left, the degree of ionization falls from 1.32 % to about 0.017 % and the pH rises from 2.88 to 4.76. That is the common ion effect. Then hydrolysis step by step: acetate makes hydroxide, ammonium makes hydronium, sodium and chloride do nothing. We sort the four types of salts with their pH formulas, pause to test washing soda, work out the pH of 0.1 M sodium acetate (8.88), show the every-salt-is-neutral trap, then an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 68 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
